newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Government approves two new charter opertors -- British Caledonian and Monarch Airways -- who will start operating flights out of London from November 1, to cater to influx of tourists expected this year, industry sources said.

Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels will soon release the remaining 37 crew of North Korean merchant vessel Morang Bong, Red Cross officials say. LTTE captured the ship off the northern Point Pedro coast on Monday night. One crew member was killed in a shootout as the rebels took control of the ship.

LTTE to release 44 of 47 Muslims abducted from eastern Erakkandi area, security sources say. The Muslims were abducted because they were suspected of giving informtion to the military about some of the rebels who escaped after a battle between the "Sea Tigers" and the navy off the eastern coast, they said.
Sri Lankan missions in London and Paris to investigate Tamil language television channels launched by Sri Lankan expatriates in those countries.
